title: Worst-Case Residual Variance Price of Covariate Balancing with Proportionally Many Gaussian Covariates
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS, but authoritative general review grades subfield below field: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4; salvageable=false, with no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: The delivered result matches the all-law trace converse with an exactly balanced, exact-budget sampler; its sharpness concerns the first-order constant, while sharp-finite-excess remains unresolved and is not overclaimed in the framing. Its causal significance is restricted to optimizing DIM under residual-only outcomes: tau is recoverable exactly from the observed outcome sum, so this is not an unavoidable causal-estimation variance price. The expected-energy constraint also permits individual assignments exceeding the requested balance level, so the theorem does not establish an optimum for threshold-based accepted-pool rerandomization. Polynomial costs hold in the declared exact real-arithmetic model, and the small examples provide no evidence that the conservative certificates become useful at practical proportional sample sizes; these scope and operational limitations constrain the paper score. The inspected [Gaussianization precursor](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.16042v1), [GSW theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/1911.03071v7), and [MFER statements](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.10497v1) do not supply the same constrained proportional equality, but the claimed distinction from Proposition 3 in the [published Gaussianization supplement](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/advance-article/doi/10.1093/jrsssb/qkag067/8660648) requires source verification because that supplement could not be retrieved independently. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Derived an exact-balanced, expected-budget sampler matching the all-law trace lower bound at first order, with deterministic public certificates and almost-sure Gaussian attainment. Math and decision reviewers passed after source attestation and related-work repairs, but the general reviewer assessed subfield rather than field (6.6 versus 7.4). Residual-only DIM scope, expected-energy rather than hard-threshold balance, ideal real-arithmetic complexity, and unresolved sharp finite excess remain; formalization was not entered.
tldr: For the fixed causal effect \(\tau\), balancing proportional covariates has a sharp worst-residual variance price for the ordinary difference in means. Conditional on frozen Gaussian covariates, the optimum over all exactly equal-arm, treatment-label-blinded laws with expected projected imbalance at most \(\rho d\) satisfies \(J_n=(n-\rho d)/(n-1-d)+o(1)\), almost surely and uniformly for every compact \(K\subset(0,1)\), \(\kappa\in K\) and \(\rho\in[1-2/\pi+\delta,1]\), with fixed positive margin \(\delta\). The limiting normalized price is \((1-\rho\kappa)/(1-\kappa)\). A calibrated Gaussian-sign law with uniform majority repair asymptotically attains the same-class trace converse. Public certificates enforce the exact finite budget, bound risk and certify polynomial real-arithmetic setup and assignment costs. Exhaustive enumeration handles remaining inputs and distinguishes feasibility from infeasibility. The sharp magnitude of the finite realizability excess remains open.
gap: Mixed-design minimax theory, GSW covariance bounds and Gaussianized optimization provide foundations and constructive bounds. The inspected results do not jointly identify an all-balanced-law residual optimum, its proportional quenched constant and an exact-budget attaining law.
fill: The headline pairs the same-class trace converse with a certified realizable design, derives uniform almost-sure Gaussian attainment and states its deterministic projection counterpart. The open question determines the optimal finite realizability correction.
